I'm 56, I only finished primary school, but I've worked these 12.4 mu for 35 years. My father taught me, and now I mostly do what I did last year, adjusting a little when I see a neighbor get better results. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so they send some money home, but I still count every yuan on inputs.

I split my land into two parts: 10 mu I rotate wheat and maize, and 2.4 mu by the house I plant cotton.

**Wheat:** Last year my wheat gave me just over 500 kg per mu. I use improved seed — the kind the dealer said is good for this area, not too expensive. I rotary till before sowing. For fertilizer, I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then topdress with half a bag of urea when the wheat turns green. That is about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 8 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I will not reduce it — fertilizer is costly, but a bad wheat harvest is a disaster. I irrigate three times: once when it turns green, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. The well has enough water. I spray three times: herbicide first, then once for rust and once for aphids. I expect 520 kg per mu if the weather holds.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize, the kind my neighbor Lao Zhang uses. I do not till for maize — I plant straight into the wheat stubble with the no-till machine. Saves diesel and time. I put about 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then side-dress with half a bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice if it does not rain: once after planting to get it up, and once when it is tasseling. Two sprays: herbicide and one for armyworm. I expect around 600 kg per mu.

**Cotton:** My 2.4 mu of cotton is harder work. I plough that plot deep because cotton roots need loose soil. I use hybrid Bt cotton seed. For fertilizer, I use one bag of compound per mu plus some extra potassium chloride because the dealer said cotton needs it for the bolls. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times — seedling, flowering, and boll stage. Cotton needs more spraying, about five times, for bollworm, aphids, and whitefly. Last year I got 250 kg per mu of seed cotton; this year I hope for 260 kg.

I do not try new tricks. If it worked last year and my neighbors do the same, I do it again.
